questions.q: On a 2.3 km route, pure VO was off by 28 m, while every map fix on the same route was off by 0.1–0.5 m. What is the fundamental difference between these two measurements?
options: VO sums increments together with their errors, while each fix is independent
VO runs at 2 Hz, while matching uses more features per frame and is therefore more accurate
The fix error also grows with distance, but 50–100 times more slowly than VO's
VO uses ORB, while matching uses a homography, which is more accurate than an affine model
questions.explain: Odometry integrates: the scale and heading errors are multiplied by the distance. Matching compares the frame with a georeferenced map afresh each time; its error is bounded by the GSD and the map's accuracy and does not depend on the distance flown.

questions.q: The bench output after one setting was changed. What error was introduced?
questions.fragment:
VO-only error [m] at distance:
     100 m ->    4.6 m (4.6 % of path)
     250 m ->   11.6 m (4.6 % of path)
     500 m ->   17.8 m (3.6 % of path)
    1000 m ->   20.8 m (2.1 % of path)
    1500 m ->   10.9 m (0.7 % of path)
options: The heading is taken by integrating frame rotation instead of from the AHRS
The height above ground is overestimated by about 5 %
The RANSAC threshold was raised from 2 to 5 px
The frame rate was lowered from 2 to 0.5 Hz
questions.explain: On the straight legs the error is a constant 4.6 % of the path: that is scale, meters = pixels · AGL / f. On a closed route it partly cancels (10.9 m at 1500 m). A heading error would give a drift that grows after the turns, not an even percentage from the first meter.

questions.q: The companion sends GPS_INPUT every 500 ms, GPS2_RAW shows fix_type = 3, but arming is refused: "PreArm: GPS 2: not healthy". What is the cause per the ArduPilot 4.6 source?
options: satellites_visible is lower than on the first receiver
horiz_accuracy is above 1 m, while EK3_GPS_CHECK requires hAcc of 1 m or better on the ground
The average message interval must be below 215 ms (about 5 Hz)
GPS_INPUT is accepted only with GPS_AUTO_SWITCH = 2 (Blend)
questions.explain: AP_GPS::is_healthy() requires average_delta_ms < 215 and no more than one consecutive late frame (> 245 ms). That is why the autopilot gets the filter's smoothed estimate at 5 Hz rather than infrequent raw fixes.

questions.q: After a change of season the inlier ratio dropped from 0.5 to 0.25. By what factor does the number of RANSAC iterations for a homography grow at the same 0.99 success probability?
options: By 2: the number of iterations is inversely proportional to the inlier ratio
By 4: the dependence is quadratic, as for a two-point estimate
It does not change: the number of iterations depends only on the pixel threshold
By roughly 16: from 72 to 1177 iterations
questions.explain: N = ln(1 − p) / ln(1 − w⁴): a homography hypothesis needs 4 correct pairs at once. w = 0.5 → 72, w = 0.25 → 1177. That is why a search window from the prediction and a strict ratio test matter more than "more features".

questions.q: In the first SITL flight without GNSS, the EKF heading differed from the true heading by 5°, and VO rotated the frame shift by that heading. The speed is 10 m/s, and over the lake there are no fixes for 22 s. How much sideways drift accumulates?
options: About 2 m: the heading affects only matching, not VO
About 19 m: 10 m/s · sin 5° · 22 s
About 110 m: 5 % of a 2.2 km path
Zero: the heading error cancels out because the EKF uses the same heading
questions.explain: The sideways drift rate v · sin δψ = 0.87 m/s, so in 22 s that is 19 m (−16 m north in the log). The EKF using the same heading does not help but hurts: the error becomes unobservable through velocity. The cure is a heading correction from the homography's residual rotation.

questions.q: VPR returned the five most similar map tiles for a frame with no position prediction. What do you do next?
options: Send the center of the best tile into GPS_INPUT with horiz_accuracy 5 m
Average the centers of the five tiles, weighted by descriptor similarity
Check each candidate with local features and a homography
Repeat the query until the same tile comes out first three frames in a row
questions.explain: A global descriptor answers "looks like", not "is located at": in the lab the correct tile came first in 40 % of queries and in the top five in 66 %. Only a geometric check gives a coordinate and the right to trust it.

questions.q: What does ArduPilot 4.6 EKF3 do with the horiz_accuracy field from GPS_INPUT?
options: Uses it as the position measurement noise, bounded between EK3_POSNE_M_NSE and 100 m
Ignores it: the position noise is always EK3_POSNE_M_NSE
Compares it with EK3_GLITCH_RAD and, when exceeded, resets the filter states to this GPS
Passes it to GPS_RAW_INT.h_acc for the GCS; it never reaches the filter
questions.explain: In AP_NavEKF3_PosVelFusion.cpp: R = sq(constrain(gpsPosAccuracy, EK3_POSNE_M_NSE, 100)). An honest σ from the vision node (1 m with fixes, 10+ m after long dead reckoning) really changes the measurement's weight; before the receiver is used, EK3_GPS_CHECK requires hAcc ≤ 5 m.

questions.q: PX4 1.18: a map-matching node outputs latitude and longitude with σ. Which EKF2 input accepts them as an absolute position?
options: MAVLink GPS_INPUT and EKF2_GPS_CTRL bit 0
The aux_global_position topic and EKF2_AGP0_CTRL bit 0
VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE and EKF2_EV_CTRL bit 3 (yaw)
ODOMETRY and EKF2_HGT_REF = 3
questions.explain: The PX4 1.18 MAVLink receiver (like 1.15–1.17) does not handle GPS_INPUT. EKF2_EV_CTRL accepts external vision in a local frame (bit 0 horizontal position, bit 3 yaw), and for global lat/lon there is aux_global_position (uXRCE-DDS /fmu/in/aux_global_position). In 1.18 there are up to four sources, each with its own EKF2_AGPn_* set: EKF2_AGP0_CTRL bit 0 (default 0, you enable it yourself), EKF2_AGP0_ID, the id of the messages to accept, EKF2_AGP0_NOISE 1.0 m and the EKF2_AGP0_GATE gate; before 1.18, a single EKF2_AGP_* set.
